main.title: Super Princess Peach
main.subtitle: Peach goes to the rescue
main.summary: Super Princess Peach is Tose's Nintendo DS platform game starring the Mushroom Kingdom's princess. Bowser has used the Vibe Scepter to capture Mario, Luigi and their companions, leaving Peach to travel through Vibe Island and bring them home. She carries Perry, a talking parasol that serves as a weapon, shield and adviser. The familiar rescue story changes hands, while the island's unusual emotional powers provide Peach with a set of actions suited to more than jumping between platforms and striking the next enemy.

cards.heading: Peach goes to the rescue
cards.text: Super Princess Peach is Tose's Nintendo DS platform game starring the Mushroom Kingdom's princess. Bowser has used the Vibe Scepter to capture Mario, Luigi and their companions, leaving Peach to travel through Vibe Island and bring them home. She carries Perry, a talking parasol that serves as a weapon, shield and adviser. The familiar rescue story changes hands, while the island's unusual emotional powers provide Peach with a set of actions suited to more than jumping between platforms and striking the next enemy.

cards.heading: Four feelings, four tools
cards.text: Peach's Vibes transform emotions into practical abilities. Joy lets her rise through the air, Rage surrounds her with fire, Gloom produces flowing tears, and Calm restores health. Each consumes the Vibe Gauge, so a useful power cannot simply remain active throughout a level. The touchscreen makes the four choices accessible while the action continues. Their uses extend beyond fighting: tears can affect plants, for example, while flight changes which ledges can be reached. Choosing an emotion becomes a way to read the surroundings.

cards.heading: A parasol with an appetite
cards.text: Perry can absorb enemies and help refill the energy needed for Peach's powers. Combat and exploration thus replenish the same small reserve, connecting an encounter to the next environmental obstacle. The adventure is organised into eight worlds containing ordinary stages and boss fights, with captured Toads hidden along the way. Searching for them gives a reason to inspect a route rather than only rush toward its exit. Peach's distinctive equipment and Vibes make the rescue an opportunity to explore another character's possibilities within a familiar platforming world.

main.title: Metroid Prime Pinball
main.subtitle: Samus becomes the ball
main.summary: Metroid Prime Pinball is Fuse Games' Nintendo DS reinterpretation of Samus Aran's first Prime adventure as a pinball game. Samus remains in Morph Ball form while familiar locations become tables filled with ramps, bumpers and enemies. The two displays form a tall playing field, and the touchscreen lets the player nudge the table to influence her path. The connection is unusually direct: an ability already central to Metroid becomes the physical object around which a different genre can be built.

cards.heading: Samus becomes the ball
cards.text: Metroid Prime Pinball is Fuse Games' Nintendo DS reinterpretation of Samus Aran's first Prime adventure as a pinball game. Samus remains in Morph Ball form while familiar locations become tables filled with ramps, bumpers and enemies. The two displays form a tall playing field, and the touchscreen lets the player nudge the table to influence her path. The connection is unusually direct: an ability already central to Metroid becomes the physical object around which a different genre can be built.

cards.heading: A table full of objectives
cards.text: Pirate Frigate and Tallon Overworld introduce a journey that opens further tables, including Phendrana Drifts and Phazon Mines. Completing objectives and minigames or defeating bosses earns artifacts. Samus can also use weapons and perform actions beyond an ordinary ball's movement, including wall jumps. That variety gives the tables tasks to pursue alongside the score. A promising shot may begin a fight, open another opportunity or advance the artifact collection, so keeping the ball alive supports a small adventure across recognisable locations.

cards.heading: Twelve artifacts and six balls
cards.text: Collecting twelve artifacts leads to the Artifact Temple, where a six-ball challenge asks the player to strike twelve targets while Meta Ridley attacks. Pinball's rising disorder becomes a suitable climax for the adapted journey. The game was also bundled with the DS Rumble Pak, adding a physical response to collisions and action. Its use of the handheld is economical: the screens provide height, the stylus supplies a nudge and the vibration gives the table an extra sense of impact without abandoning the familiar flippers.

main.title: Call of Duty 2
main.subtitle: The war unfolds across three Allied fronts
main.summary: Infinity Ward follows Soviet, British and American soldiers through larger battles, with regenerating health and squads that react to the fighting around them.

cards.heading: From the Soviet front to North Africa and Normandy
cards.text: Call of Duty 2 first reached Windows on 25 October 2005. Developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision, it returns to the Second World War through Soviet, British and American perspectives. Its campaigns move between ruined Russian cities, the North African desert and the Normandy landings, including the Rangers' assault on Pointe du Hoc. The Xbox 360 edition followed as a launch title in November, bringing the same main game to Microsoft's new console rather than adapting the separate Big Red One campaign.

cards.heading: Taking cover replaces the search for health packs
cards.text: The sequel replaces health packs with recovery after the player escapes enemy fire. A reddening screen and a louder heartbeat warn of serious injury, while a nearby-grenade indicator gives another reason to move quickly. Soldiers can carry two firearms, use their iron sights and throw fragmentation or smoke grenades. Smoke can conceal an advance across exposed ground, and some missions change the scale of the action by placing the player in a tank.

cards.heading: Squad voices make the battlefield easier to read
cards.text: The new engine fills battles with more soldiers, vehicles, explosions and weather effects. Squad members also help explain what is happening through context-sensitive battle chatter: they warn about approaching enemies, identify hostile fire and react as the situation changes. Allies use cover and lay down supporting fire around the player. This combination of visual spectacle and shouted information makes the battlefield feel crowded while still giving the player clues about where danger is coming from.

main.title: Civilization IV
main.summary: Civilization IV (also known as Sid Meier's Civilization IV) is a 2005 4X turn-based strategy video game developed by Firaxis Games and published by 2K.

cards.heading: Soren Johnson leads the fourth Civilization
cards.text: Civilization IV (also known as Sid Meier's Civilization IV) is a 2005 4X turn-based strategy video game developed by Firaxis Games and published by 2K. It is the fourth installment of the Civilization series and was designed by Soren Johnson. It was released in North America, Europe, and Australia, between October 25 and November 4, 2005, and followed by Civilization V.

cards.heading: Choosing a route to victory
cards.text: Civilization IV begins with limited resources and a small settlement, usually in 4000 BC. Over successive turns, the player builds an empire and chooses a route to victory. Conquest and control of territory offer military approaches; launching a ship to Alpha Centauri rewards technological progress. Developing three cities to legendary cultural status or winning a United Nations leadership vote provides other goals. A time limit can instead settle the result by score. The game also introduced a new visual engine based on Gamebryo, changing how that growing world was presented.

cards.heading: Baba Yetu, expansions and reception
cards.text: The game has received critical acclaim and was hailed as an exemplary product of one of the leading video game producers in the turn-based strategy genre, and has been listed as one of the best video games of all time. Civilization IV sold over 3 million copies by 2008 and won multiple awards, including several Game of the Year awards. Its title song, "Baba Yetu", was the first piece of video game music to win a Grammy Award. Two major expansions were released, Civilization IV: Warlords and Civilization IV: Beyond the Sword, as well as the stand-alone expansion pack Civilization IV: Colonization, which were all combined in 2009 into one release edition titled Sid Meier's Civilization IV: The Complete Edition.

main.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories
main.subtitle: An Entire City Fits in Your Pocket
main.summary: On October 24, 2005, Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories was released in North America on PlayStation Portable.

cards.heading: A new Liberty City story on PSP
cards.text: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories brought a new adventure in Liberty City to PlayStation Portable on October 24, 2005 in North America. Rockstar Leeds worked with Rockstar North on the game, using the geography of Grand Theft AutoIII for a story set earlier, in 1998. New missions, characters and activities accompany the return. Traffic, pedestrians, radio and travel between districts run on the handheld, which also offers local wireless multiplayer for up to six people.

cards.heading: Loading the city from UMD
cards.text: Liberty City Stories continually loads the city from the PSP's UMD while managing traffic, pedestrians, missions and radio. Reviews noted pauses and slowdowns when vehicles or audio streams changed quickly. These were visible limits of fitting a large three-dimensional city onto the handheld. Rockstar Leeds kept the familiar pattern of travelling through an active city and moving between activities within it.

cards.heading: Returning to the city in 1998
cards.text: Toni Cipriani travels through the Liberty City of 1998, before the events of Grand Theft AutoIII. Streets and districts remain recognisable, while buildings, activities and relationships show an earlier period. Returning players can compare the city with the one they remember from 2001. The shared geography gives that comparison a place in the journey, adding another reason to notice a familiar location.

cards.heading: Six players through local wireless
cards.text: Up to six players can connect nearby PSPs through ad hoc wireless play. Deathmatches, races and vehicle-based modes use sections of the city as their arenas. Each participant needs the game and a PSP within range of the others. For a group gathered in the same place, the handheld offers a shared version of streets normally explored alone.

main.title: Star Wars: Battlefront II
main.summary: Star Wars: Battlefront II is a 2005 first and third-person shooter video game based on the Star Wars film franchise.

cards.heading: A soldier's view of the Star Wars battles
cards.text: Star Wars: Battlefront II is Pandemic Studios' 2005 first- and third-person shooter, published by LucasArts. The sequel takes players into battles from the film series on PlayStation 2, Windows and Xbox, with a PSP version developed by Savage Entertainment. Its campaign follows a veteran soldier whose service spans the Galactic Republic and the Galactic Empire. The game first reached PAL territories on October 28 and North America on November 1.

cards.heading: Jedi, Sith and battles in space
cards.text: The game features new vehicles, characters, game mechanics, maps, and missions compared to the original Battlefront. Unlike its predecessor, Battlefront II features a more narrative-based campaign, retelling portions of the Star Wars story from the point of view of a veteran clone Imperial Stormtrooper, reminiscing about his tour of duty in service of both the Galactic Republic and the Galactic Empire. Gameplay additions over Battlefront include the use of Jedi and Sith, additional game modes such as hero assault, and objective-based space battles.

cards.heading: Keeping an online favourite playable
cards.text: Battlefront II was well received, with particular praise for its campaign, and sold six million copies by 2007. Online play later faced the closure of GameSpy, leading to support through services including GameRanger. In October 2017, multiplayer returned to the Windows version with Steam and GOG cross-play. The Xbox edition gained compatibility with later Xbox consoles and online play through Insignia. The original and its predecessor returned together in the 2024 Battlefront Classic Collection.

main.title: From Russia with Love
main.summary: From Russia with Love is a 2005 third-person shooter game developed by EA Redwood Shores and published by Electronic Arts (EA).

cards.heading: From Russia with Love
cards.text: From Russia with Love is a 2005 third-person shooter game developed by EA Redwood Shores and published by Electronic Arts (EA). It is based on the 1963 James Bond film of the same name but with several changes, including additional characters, locations, and a different villainous organisation. Additionally, it features elements of later Bond films such as the Aston Martin DB5 that debuted in Goldfinger (1964) and the jet pack from Thunderball (1965).

cards.heading: Making the game
cards.text: From Russia with Love is notable in that it is the only video game to use Sean Connery's younger likeness as James Bond and the first to include all new voice work by the actor after twenty-two years away from the role, marking his eighth and final performance as Bond across any medium before his death in 2020. From Russia with Love is also the last James Bond video game developed or published by Electronic Arts before they lost the rights to Activision in 2006.

cards.heading: Reception and legacy
cards.text: From Russia with Love was released for GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox in November 2005. A PlayStation Portable (PSP) version was released in April 2006. The game received mixed reviews from critics.
